title: Intro to Color Theory
description: A short course on color theory basics for illustration.

items.title: What is the color wheel?
items.body:
The color wheel is a circular diagram that arranges colors according to their chromatic relationship.

Primary colors — red, blue, and yellow — sit at equal distances around the wheel. Every other color on the wheel is mixed from these three.

items.title: Draw a color wheel
items.description: Create your own 12-color wheel using any medium (digital or traditional). Take a photo or export it, then upload it here.

items.title: Complementary colors
items.body:
Complementary colors sit directly opposite each other on the color wheel — for example, red and green, or blue and orange.

When placed next to each other, complementary colors create the strongest possible contrast, which is why they're often used to make a subject pop.

items.title: Identify complementary pairs
items.description: Find 5 complementary color pairs in photos, artwork, or objects around you and list them.

items.title: Analogous color schemes
items.body: Analogous colors sit next to each other on the wheel (e.g. yellow, yellow-green, and green). They create harmonious, low-contrast palettes that feel calm and cohesive.

items.title: Build an analogous palette
items.description: Pick a 3-color analogous palette and apply it to a simple shape or illustration. Upload the result.
